findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed a bag of guacamole to be stored in a container of cut tomatoes. Discussed with PIC, education was provided on proper storage of items and tomatoes were discarded. Ensure any TCS item is properly stored in a way that prevents any possible contamination.
findings.citation_text: 3-305.11(A) Food Storage. (A) Except as specified in (B) and (C) of this section, FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: Upon arrival, inspector observed staff going through coolers disposing off TCS items held past 7 day date marking maximum. Discussed with PIC, date marking education was provided and remaining TCS items were pulled and discarded. Ensure all TCS items are properly date marked and pulled after their 7 day date marking maximum.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display.
findings.comment: Observed multiple food items kept in walk in cooler and freezer to be resting on a pan on floor. Discussed with PIC, education was provided and items were moved to at least 6 inches off floor. Ensure all food items are stored at least 6 inches off of floor.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
(Repeat x2) Observed multiple containers holding various TCS foods to be held past their 7 day maximum. Discussed with PIC, items were pulled and discarded. Ensure containers are properly date marked and that staff are checking the dates frequently. 

3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed multiple knives being stored on faucet of covered sink. Discussed with PIC, knives were washed and stored on magnetic strip on wall. Ensure knives are being stored in a way to prevent contamination. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
REPEAT: Observed multiple containers holding various meats, homemade sauces, vegetables, and fruit to be held past their 7 day maximum holding. Multiple containers were also thrown out due to no label being present. Discussed with PIC and items were discarded. Ensure containers are properly date marked and that staff are checking the dates frequently.

If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
Observed multiple knives being stored on faucet of covered sink. Discussed with PIC and knives were washed and stored on magnetic strip on wall. Ensure knives are being stored in a way to prevent contamination. 

3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
5-205.11: (A) A HANDWASHING SINK shall be maintained so that it is accessible at all times for EMPLOYEE use. (B) A HANDWASHING SINK may not be used for purposes other than handwashing. (C) An automatic handwashing facility shall be used in accordance with manufacturer’s instructions. 

Observed the upstairs bar hand sink to be blocked by a sani bucket. Cease practice. Hand sinks are for hand washing only. Ensure staff is aware to keep sani buckets out of the sink in order to contribute towards frequent hand washing. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria: (A) chlorine shall have minimum temperature (55F), concentration (100ppm), and pH (10). (B) Iodine shall have 68F, pH of 5 or less and concentration of 12.5ppm and 25ppm. (C) Quaternary ammonium shall have 75F, concentration based on label, and water with 500ppm hardness or less. (D) - (E) Meets EPA-label use and regulatory authority approval. (P) (F) Other chemical sanitzers in-use shall have EPA-registered label, display device registration number on devide and is operated and maintained in accordance with manufacturers instructions (Pf)

Observed the upstairs sani bucket at the bar (that was in the hand sink - see violation #10) to be 0 ppm. PIC asked waitress if the bucket was re-made today. It appears the sani bucket was from the day before. Ensure staff is aware that sani buckets should be frequently changed out to maintain concentration - every 4 hours or so. Quaternary ammonium (sanitizer type facility is using) should be maintained at 200-400 ppm. Facility has test strips to verify concentrations of sanitizer. Ensure staff frequently changes sani buckets and utilizes test strips to verify concentration ranges. Discussed with PIC. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

(REPEAT) Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. The can opener blade in the kitchen (attached to a prep table) was soiled. Employee stated she had not used the can opener today. Ensure staff cleans can opener blades every 4 hours or as needed to maintain a clean blade. Discussed with staff. Can opener blade was brought to the dish machine to wash, rinse, sanitize. COS.
2. The ceiling vent above the dish machine area where clean utensils are stored has dust on it. Clean. Repeat violation since last routine inspection on 2/15/23.
3. The clean cooking utensil shelf under the large vent at the rear kitchen hand sink has a layer of visible dust hanging from the grates. The vent above it previously was very dusty and blew the dust over the clean cooking utensils. Ensure the vent and shelving unit is frequently cleaned to prevent dust (should not be dusty where clean utensils are stored).
4. Main level bar soda gun holder was soiled with mold. Discussed with PIC. Employee washed, rinsed, and sanitized. COS.
5. Upstairs bar had a moldy soda nozzle. Inspector showed PIC. Employee washed, rinsed, and sanitized. COS. 
6. The ice machine in the kitchen had a layer of mold along the interior baffle. Inspector showed main CFPM for kitchen. Facility began pulling all the ice from the machine in order to wash, rinse, sanitize the interior basin and ceiling, plus baffle. COS.

Discussed the above food-contact surfaces with PIC. Ensure routine cleaning is observed in order to prevent mold, debris, food splash, etc. accumulation. Inspector will follow-up regarding the above areas on 10/16/23.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.112: (A) Temperature of the fresh hot water SANITIZING rinse may not be more than 194F or less than 165F for stationary rack, single temperature machines. All other machines can be no less than 180F. (B) Maximum temperature does not apply to high pressure and temperature systems with wand-type spraying devices. 

Observed the upstairs bar heated dish machine to maintain 154F after multiple runs. Facility has a maximum registering thermometer as well. Both Inspector’s heat thermometer and the facility’s could not get a temperature reading past 154F. Facility will have maintenance check the machine. Discussed with PIC not to use the heated dish machine at the upstairs bar until it is running at least 160F. Utilize the 3 compartment sink to wash, rinse, sanitize. Inspector will follow-up on 10/16/23.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.18: (A) FOOD shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time criteria. If container or PACKAGE does not bear a date or day or if inappropriately marked with date or day exceeding temperature and time combination. (B) Refrigerated RTE TCS FOOD prepared in FOOD ESTABLISHMENT and dispensed through vending machine shall be discarded if exceeding temperature and time. 

Observed the reach-in cooler across from the fryers to have 8-day old calamari (dated 9/28/23). Observed the walk-in cooler to have 8-day old cooked/cooled pasta (9/28) and several day old creme brlée (9/24). Discussed with PIC. Ensure that staff goes through the coolers and discards items with over a 7-day date marking. All items were voluntarily discarded. Date marking otherwise was very good. Continue to check daily in order to dispose of expired foods. COS.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (B) The FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of cooking EQUIPMENT and pans shall be kept free of encrusted grease deposits and other soil accumulations. (C) NonFOOD-CONTACT SURFACES of EQUIPMENT shall be kept free of an accumulation of dust, dirt, FOOD residue, and other debris.

Observed the following non-food contact surfaces in need of cleaning:
1. There is quite a bit of grease build-up inside the fryers and on the fryer interior doors, as well as underneath the fryers. Ensure staff routine de-greases the fryer stations and wash, rinse, sanitizes.
2. Walk-in cooler fan has a slight accumulation of dust.
3. Baffles of the hood system in the kitchen have a slight accumulation of grease debris build-up. Meacham is due out for service.

Discussed routine cleaning with PIC. Ensure staff is aware to clean as needed to prevent dust/debris/grease/food splash accumulation. Ensure the above areas are cleaned before the next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

(REPEAT) Observed no food handler’s licenses for the kitchen staff. There were several people during the inspection working in the kitchen. PIC could only provide two CFPM’s licenses. Ensure all kitchen staff as a valid food handler’s license (valid for 3 years). Ensure copies are left at the facility. Correct before the next routine inspection. Discussed with PIC. This is a repeat violation since the last routine inspection on 2/15/23.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: (A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED. 

Upon beginning of inspection, employee was ahead of Inspector washing hands. Employee did not utilize a barrier to turn off the faucet after washing hands (cross contamination). Discussed with PIC and employee. Ensure proper hand washing technique is adhered to: hot water, soap, lather for 20 seconds, wash hands, dry hands, utilize a barrier such as a paper towel to turn off faucet handles after washing hands. COS.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-601.11: (A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch. 

Observed the following food-contact areas in need of cleaning (wash, rinse, sanitize):
1. Multiple ceiling vents and tiles are covered in dust. Dust is visibly blowing with fans on. Area is above the main prep line. Ensure ceilings are routinely cleaned as they are directly accumulating dust above the food preparation surfaces. 
2. Large vent next to the back kitchen hand sink has an accumulation of dust. Vent is blowing directly over clean cooking utensils. Clean the vent to prevent dust build-up.

Discussed routine cleaning of areas where food preparation is occurring and/or clean cooking utensils are stored. Inspector will follow-up regarding the above two issues on 2/27/23.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.comment:
4-204.112: (A) In refrigerated or hot FOOD storage unit, TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE shall be located to measure air temperature. (B) EQUIPMENT holding TCS FOOD shall have TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICE affixed to device. (C) Does not apply to EQUIPMENT without practical means of measuring ambient air surroundings. (D) TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall be designed to be easily readable. C (E) FOOD and water TEMPERATURE MEASURING DEVICES shall have numerical scale, printed record, or digital readout in increments no greater than 1C or 2F in the intended range of use. Pf

Observed multiple coolers to lack thermometers. Several were provided thermometers. Ensure all cold holding units have thermometers within them to measure air temperature of unit. Ensure extra thermometers are kept at the facility to have as back-up. Discussed with PIC. Purchase before next routine inspection.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-201.11: Except as specified under § 6-201.14 and except for antislip floor coverings or applications that may be used for safety reasons, floors, floor coverings, walls, wall coverings, and ceilings shall be designed, constructed, and installed so they are SMOOTH and EASILY CLEANABLE. 

Observed the following areas in need of repairs (no longer smooth, easily cleanable, or non-absorbent):
1. Caulk is needed in the following areas due to being molded (water exposure), missing, and/or coming away: rear kitchen hand sinks near dish machine area, employee bathroom hand sink in kitchen, 3 compartment sink area, dish machine area, downstairs bar hand sink and bar 3 compartment sink. Ensure all areas have moldy and/or teared caulking replaced. Ensure missing caulking is provided.
2. The flooring in the dry storage area near the employee bathroom in the kitchen is broken into many pieces. Replace the tiling in this area.
3. Ceiling tiles above the spray nozzle area by dish machine in kitchen are soiled from water damage. Replace the damaged ceiling tiles.

Discussed repairs with PIC. Ensure maintenance staff addresses the above issues. Ensure repairs before next routine inspection.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.  

Observed the only non-CFPM to have an expired food handler’s license. Discussed with PIC. Ensure employee completes food handler’s training and certification before the next routine inspection. Keep copies at the facility. License is valid for 3 years. Ensure new hires complete the training as a part of onboarding procedures.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625/3.07 Sec. 3.07. Allergen awareness training. (b) Unless otherwise provided, all certified food service sanitation managers employed by a restaurant must receive or obtain training in basic allergen awareness principles within 30 days after employment and every 3 years thereafter.

Observed the only allergen training certification to be expired (main chef’s). Ensure all certified food protection manager’s (CFPM’s) have completed allergen training certification and that the certificate remains valid. Allergen training certification is valid for 3 years. Provided educational hand out for the PIC in order to have his staff complete the certification. Ensure all CFPM’s complete before next routine inspection. Keep copies of certification at the facility.

findings.title: Food in good condition, safe, and unadulterated
findings.comment:
3-202.15: FOOD packages shall be in good condition and protect the integrity of the contents so that the FOOD is not exposed to ADULTERATION or potential contaminants. 

Two cans on the can rack (mixed veggies and Monterey Jack salsa) are observed with major dents in the upper and lower seams of the can. Inspector discussed with the PIC and reviewed that cans with significant dents in the three seams (top, bottoms or side), or cans with major dents in the non-seam sides should be separated for credit/discard. The cans were removed during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

Half of the sani buckets in the kitchen are observed to barely register a change on the inspector’s test strips. The other half show right around 200 ppm quaternary ammonium. Buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-904.11: (A) cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed to prevent FOOD- and lip-contact surface contamination. (B) UTENSILS not prewrapped shall be presented so only handles are touched by EMPLOYEES and/or CONSUMERS. (C) SINGLE-SERVCIE ARTICLES intended for FOOD- and lip-contact shall be furnished for CONSUMER with wrapper or APPROVED dispenser. 

A pair of containers on the shelf above the prep line corner are observed with spoons and wooden pot stickers mixed in with pens, markers  and highlighters. These items are generally not considered cleaned/sanitized surfaces and should remain separated from food contact items. The pot stickers were discarded and the spoons moved to dish for cleaning. Moving foreword the food contact items should be stored separately from the non-food contact items (separate containers suggested).

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.comment:
3-302.11: (A) (1)-(2) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display (P). (3) FOOD shall be protected from cross contamination by cleaning visibly soiled containers, removing damaged containers, separating washed and unwashed produce (C).  

Two locations in the walk in cooler had raw beef stored over raw fish/ seafood. PIC moved the items during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

1) On arrival, the dish machine was not registering on either the inspector’s or the facility’s test strips. 2) On arrival the sani buckets in the facility are observed low on both the inspector’s and facility’s test strips. Investigation shows that the solution coming out of the dispenser is low. 
EcoLab was contacted for both situations and arrived during the inspection for maintenance.  After maintenance, the dish machine is now producing effective levels of CL for food contact sanitizing. The dispenser for the sani buckets is going to require a different line for water (it is currently to hot) to be installed. PIC will notify inspector when this has taken place for a spot check to be conducted. Until that time, buckets will be made manually using quat tablets.

findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible
findings.comment:
6-301.12: Each HANDWASHING SINK shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; (C) A heated-air hand drying device; (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures. 

Paper towels were not available at the hand sink in the upstairs bar area. PIC was consulted and paper towel supplied during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment:
3-501.17: (A) Except for ROP, Refrigerated, RTE, TCS Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date/maximum of 7 days. Day of preparation is Day 1 (Pf). (B) Date marking may not exceed manufacturer’s use-by date (Pf).

Opened and partially used gallons of milk are observed in both the downstairs and upstairs bar areas without date marking. PIC was consulted and date marks added during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. (B) clean EQUIPMENT shall be stored in self-draining position that allows air drying, covered or inverted. (D) Items that are kept in closed PACKAGES may be stored below 6 inches if on dollies, pallets, racks, and skids properly designed. 

A partial box of potatoes is observed stored directly on top of cleaned lids on the shelves across from the ice machine. PIC was consulted and the box moved down a shelf to its correct location. The lids were also washed during the inspection.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.comment:
4-501.114: Chemical sanitizer for manual or mechanical operation shall meet proper criteria.

On arrival, all of the sani buckets in the kitchen area (4 observed) registered 0 ppm quat on the inspector's test strips. The buckets were remade during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment:
4-903.11: (A) clean FOOD-CONTACT surfaces shall be stored: in clean, dry location, not exposed to splash or other contamination, and at least 6 inches above floor. 

In the bar area, multiple storage bin in the ice chests used for Styrofoam cups and drink mixing utensils are observed soiled. PIC moved the items to dish for cleaning and discarded the single service items in the.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) Food contact surfaces should be clean to sight and touch. The left soda gun in the upstairs bar area is observe with black substance coating 2 of the inner spouts. A thin line was also observed under the nozzle and around the circumference. The gun was cleaned during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. 1) A container of cottage cheese was observed in the four door cooler as you come into the kitchen without a date marking. The cottage cheese was discarded during the inspection.  2) A square container of cheese sauce in the walk in cooler was observed with a date mark of 2/24. This makes today day ten of the allowed 7. The sauce was discarded during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized
findings.citation_text: 4-601.11(A)  (Pf) The potatoes slicer in the kitchen was observed soiled during the inspection. The slicer was moved to cleaning during the inspection.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Cleaned utensils are observed stored in soiled containers: 1) large mixers under the prep table in the kitchen, 2) condiment bottles next to the dish area in the kitchen, 3) drink mixers and utensils at the north end of the downstairs bar. All utensils and their containers were moved to cleaning during the inspection to correct.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-501.14  (C) Intake air vent above clean food service items next to the hand sink were found with accumulation of dust on them. Intake and exhaust air ducts shall be cleaned and filters changed so they are not a source of contamination by dust, dirt, and other materials. Clean prior to the next routine inspection.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text:
3-501.17 (A) (Pf) Refrigerated, READY-TOEAT, TIME/TEMPERATURE CONTROL FOR SAFETY FOOD prepared and held in a FOOD ESTABLISHMENT for more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the FOOD shall be consumed on the PREMISES, sold, or discarded.

Items in the multi door cooler at the end of the prep line had date marks exceding the 7 day limit (scallion aoli with 3/14 and diced onions with 3/7). Items were discarded during the inspection.

findings.title: Contamination prevented during food preparation, storage and display
findings.citation_text:
3-305.11 (A) (C) FOOD shall be protected from contamination by storing the FOOD: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where it is not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.

Foods were observed stored on the floor in both the walk in cooler and the walk in freezer. Discussed with the PIC and instructed them to stored foods off the floor.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.citation_text:
4-903.11 (A) (C) Cleaned EQUIPMENT and UTENSILS, laundered LINENS, and SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLEUSE ARTICLES shall be stored: (1) In a clean, dry location; (2) Where they are not exposed to splash, dust, or other contamination; and (3) At least 15 cm (6 inches) above the floor.
Clean utensils were stroed in containers that had general dust and debris in the bottoms. The situation was discussed with the PIC and they were instructed to store cleaned items in cotainers that are also maintained clean.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the ice cream freezer to have frost buildup.  Defrost the freezer to make it a smooth and easily cleanable surface.
750-600 Non-food contact surfaces shall be smooth and easily cleanable

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces clean
findings.comment:
Observed the inside of the microwave on the north side of the kitchen to be soiled.  Clean the microwave.
750-800e Non-food contact surfaces of equipment shall be cleaned as often as is necessary to keep the equipment free of accumulation of dust, dirt, food particles, and other debris.

findings.title: Walls, ceilings, and attached equipment, properly constructed, clean
findings.comment:
1. (REPEAT) Observed the north side wall of the kitchen near the handsink to have food splash.  Clean the wall. 2.Observed heavy dust accumulation on the hood system baffles.  Clean the baffles.  Clean the walls and ceilings.
750-1220 Walls, ceilings, and attached fixtures shall be kept clean. Clean the walls and ceilings.
